editorial.tldr: This page mechanically groups ten items that share the phrase "large language models" in their title, not one developing story. It runs from three unrelated anomaly-detection papers (Aug 24-25) through a hallucination-detection line, an agent-swarm benchmark, an HVAC deployment review, and a Zhipu/MiniMax business-model roundup, with nothing connecting them but that phrase.
editorial.whats_new: A recluster pulled in three older, unrelated anomaly-detection papers (Aug 24-25); the newest dated item is still Sep 10's domain-specific hallucination detector combining fine-tuned DeBERTa-v3 classification with Monte Carlo sampling.
editorial.why_it_matters: Ranking-by-shared-title-phrase can silently fold unrelated arxiv papers and business news into one page -- treat this grouping as noise, not corroboration, before citing more than one item from it together.
editorial.take_for_builders: Don't treat a shared link on this page as corroboration across sources -- these items are grouped by word overlap only; verify each independently before citing them together.

open_questions: Does PoP's detection rate hold against sampling-based baselines such as semantic entropy, and at what accuracy cost?
Do PoP's inter-layer activation features transfer across model families, or must a detector be trained per model?
Does activation-level detection need weights access, ruling it out for API-only deployments?
Does SwarmBench report results for today's popular agent frameworks, or only for research prototypes?
Does the DeBERTa-v3 domain-specific hallucination detector generalize across domains, or need per-domain fine-tuning?
